subject: Private Endpoint allowlist and outbound routing — signoff & proxy requirements
body:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private endpoint allowlist and outbound routing details

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Security wants a concise list of network requirements for our private endpoint so we can feed them into our change control and firewall change request. Two asks: a) a definitive set of IPs/FQDNs and ports Redwood requires from our perimeter to reach the control plane, and b) guidance on whether we need an outbound TLS proxy / SNI-preserving egress device so the team can add it to the procurement ticket.

Attached is our standard evidence template (acme_allowlist_requirements.pdf). If you can return the allowlist CSV and an ops note on proxy behavior we can schedule a change window. Also flag anything that would break our egress-only model (no inbound).

Sam Turner
Director, Cloud Security
Acme Health

---

On Tue, 10 Feb 2026 at 10:30 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoint allowlist and outbound routing details

Hi Sam —

Appreciate the template. High-level answers up front:
- Control plane endpoints: we publish a small set of static egress IPs for the control plane (see attached CSV).
- Ports: TCP 443 outbound to those IPs; we recommend allowing TLS (no layer 7 termination) to preserve mTLS and certificate validation.
- Proxy: a transparent TLS-proxy that performs SNI-preserving passthrough is acceptable; we do not require TLS interception or certificate re-issuance.

Details and caveats below — Laura, Vanessa, Neha: tagging you for ops/console implications and the CSV signoff.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

On Wed, 11 Feb 2026 at 09:05 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoint allowlist and outbound routing details

Sam / Marcus —

Adding the operational details from the Private deployment team and a short checklist for Acme's change request: 

1) Required egress endpoints (summary):
   - Control plane IP block (primary): 52.19.112.24
   - Control plane IP block (secondary/failover): 52.19.112.25
   - S3-compatible artifact store (region-specific): artifacts.redwood-inference.com -> resolve to region A records (we provide CNAMEs)
   - DNS: allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 to your forwarding resolvers for lookups (we don't require direct DNS to our hosts)

2) Ports/Protocols:
   - Outbound TCP 443 to the control plane and artifact endpoints
   - Outbound TCP 80 only for health handshake to artifact CDN (optional, prefer 443)

3) Proxy requirements and behavior:
   - TLS must be end-to-end for API traffic. Redwood authenticates using mutual TLS where configured (we provision client certs if requested).
   - If you place an egress TLS proxy that performs SNI-preserving passthrough (TCP-level proxy), that is fine.
   - If your proxy terminates TLS and re-encrypts with a new cert, ensure it preserves client certificate forwarding (X-Forwarded-Client-Cert or a separate mTLS key exchange) — we prefer to avoid this pattern.

4) NAT/Source IP considerations:
   - We require a stable set of source IPs for the private endpoint to be allowlisted (we will not accept ephemeral NAT ranges without pre-approval).
   - If you use an egress gateway, please allocate a small set (<=4) of static IPs and include reverse DNS entries where possible.

5) Audit evidence we can provide:
   - Signed control-plane TLS certificate fingerprint
   - Timestamped connection logs for the onboarding window

Attachments: redwood-proxy-ip-list.csv (contains the IPs above plus a short expiry note).

Next steps (requested from Acme):
- Confirm whether your egress gateway will preserve SNI/TCP passthrough or terminate TLS.
- Provide change window and NAT IPs if you are using a gateway.
- Confirm whether you need us to issue client certs for mTLS or prefer token-based TLS client auth.

Happy to join a quick call if helpful.

-Laura
Principal Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Thu, 12 Feb 2026 at 16:47 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoint allowlist and outbound routing details

Sam —

Thanks — Acme's change board confirmed they will use an egress gateway with TLS passthrough (no termination) and will allocate three static NAT IPs for outbound. They attached the planned NAT IP block in the change ticket and asked us to confirm the CSV.

I attached a signed CSV (redwood-proxy-ip-list.csv) with the following rows: 52.19.112.24, 52.19.112.25, artifacts.redwood-inference.com, TCP/443. We added a note: "Do not perform TLS interception; preserve SNI; permit outbound DNS to resolvers."

We also confirmed with product that token-based client auth is acceptable for this deployment; mTLS is optional. I'll drop this CSV and a short runbook into the shared Drive link (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/rdw-private-acme) for the Acme ops team and mark the onboarding ticket as ready for scheduling.

Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

- acme_allowlist_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)
